newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Brittan, Barshefsky get closer to infotech pact.
newsitem.headline: Brittan, Barshefsky get closer to infotech pact.

text.p: European Union (EU) Trade Commisssioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Tuesday the EU and the United States, as well Canada and Japan, were making progress in solving differences over a global agreement on information technology, and hoped to continue progress in talks later in the afternoon.
After a luncheon meeting of the four major trading partners, Brittan told reporters: "We are making a lot of progress and we hope to make further progress this afternoon."

Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefksy said she concurred with Brittan's comments, but declined to say anything more on the proposed pact to elminate tariffs on computers and telecoms products by 2000.
Intense negotiations on the issue have been going on during the first two days of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting that opened in Singapore on Monday.

The hope is to wrap up an agreement between the major trading partners on infotech as quickly as possible in order to convince Asian trading partners to sign on to the agreement by the end of this week's WTO meeting.
